Roasted Corn

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 4Prep 10 minCook 20 min

Roasted Corn is a beloved traditional dish served during the Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa, celebrated in Haitian Vodou culture. This simple yet flavorful treat honors Papa Zaka, the spirit of agriculture and the harvest, symbolizing gratitude for the earth's bounty.

Ingredients

  • 4 ears of fresh corn, husked
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter (28 g), melted
  • 1 teaspoon sea salt (5 g)
  • 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper (1 g)
  • 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika (1 g)
  • Optional: chopped fresh parsley for garnish

Method

  1. Preheat your grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
  2. Brush each ear of corn with melted butter, ensuring even coverage.
  3. Sprinkle sea salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika evenly over the corn.
  4. Place the corn on the grill and cook, turning every 5 minutes, until all sides are lightly charred and the kernels are tender, about 15-20 minutes.
  5. Remove the corn from the grill and, if desired, garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

Tips

  • For a smoky flavor, use a charcoal grill instead of gas.
  • If fresh corn is unavailable, thawed frozen corn on the cob can be used.
  • Add a squeeze of fresh lime juice before serving for a zesty twist.
